name: Guinea
summary: Red, yellow and green vertical bands. Adopted in 1958, when Guinea became the first French colony in sub-Saharan Africa to reject the French Community and take full independence, it follows Ghana's example in using the Pan-African colours.
origin: In the 1958 referendum on the French Community, Guinea under Ahmed Sékou Touré voted 'No' and became independent on 2 October 1958. Its flag combined the colours of Ghana, with which it formed a short-lived union, in the French vertical style.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Work, and the sacrifice of the people in the struggle against colonialism.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: Justice, and the gold and sun of Guinea.

facts: The three colours match the national motto 'Travail, Justice, Solidarité' (Work, Justice, Solidarity).
Mali's flag is the same in reverse order.
Guinea was the first French African colony to become independent outside the French Community.
clues: Red, yellow and green vertical bands.
